title: Pennsylvania Seller Disclosure (No Mandated Form)
description: Pennsylvania Real Estate Disclosure Law (68 Pa. C.S. §7301) requires sellers to complete a disclosure statement, but there is NO state-mandated form — brokers use PAR standard form or their own. This is unusual: PA mandates disclosure but not the specific form. The State Real Estate Commission disclosure form content is described at 49 Pa. Code §35.335a.

required_actions.note: No state-mandated form. PAR Form SPD or broker-specific form acceptable. Must be signed before contract.

metadata.unusual: PA mandates disclosure but not a specific form.

title: Pennsylvania Realty Transfer Tax
description: Pennsylvania 1% state RTT split equally between buyer and seller (0.5% each), plus local transfer tax typically 1% split. Philadelphia imposes ~4.278% total.

required_actions.note: State RTT is 1% (split). Verify local RTT with municipality.

title: Consumer Notice (Agency Disclosure)
description: Under the Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act (RELRA), 63 P.S. §455.608, and 49 Pa. Code §35.336, every broker, associate broker and salesperson must provide the 'Consumer Notice' disclosure summary to a consumer at the initial interview. The notice explains the available business relationships (seller agency, buyer agency, dual agency, designated agency, and transaction licensee) established by Act 112 of 1998, the statutory duties owed under §606.1 (63 P.S. §455.606a), and cautions the consumer not to disclose confidential information until a relationship has been selected. The consumer signs an acknowledgement of receipt.

required_actions.note: Deliver at the initial interview before discussing the consumer's motivation or confidential information; obtain signed acknowledgement.

title: Title/Settlement Agent Closing (Attorney Not Required)
description: Pennsylvania is not an attorney-closing state. Real estate settlements are routinely conducted by licensed title insurance companies or settlement agents, and no attorney is required to be present. Either party may retain counsel, but engaging a settlement/title agent to handle the closing, title search, title insurance, and recording is the standard practice.

required_actions.note: Engage a licensed title/settlement agent to conduct closing, issue title insurance, and record the deed. Attorney involvement is optional in PA.

citations: 40 P.S. §910-1 et seq. (Title Insurance Companies Act)

metadata.note: Attorney not required; included to document PA closing practice for the engine's closing-category coverage.

title: Bituminous Coal Mine Subsidence Notice
description: For property located in Pennsylvania's bituminous coal regions (primarily western and southwestern PA) where coal or subsurface support rights have been severed from the surface estate, the deed and agreement of sale must contain the statutory coal/mine subsidence notice under the Bituminous Mine Subsidence and Land Conservation Act, 52 P.S. §1406.14. The notice warns the buyer that the coal may be owned by another party and that surface structures may not be entitled to support — meaning lawful mining beneath the property could cause subsidence damage without recourse. No notice is required where the title search shows no severed coal estate or the property lies outside the bituminous coal fields. Sellers should also direct buyers to DEP Mine Subsidence Insurance Fund maps.

required_actions.note: Include the statutory coal/mine subsidence notice in the agreement of sale and deed when a severed coal estate exists.
Refer buyer to PA DEP Mine Subsidence Insurance Fund maps; mining beneath the surface may occur without liability for subsidence damage.

citations: 52 P.S. §1406.14 (Bituminous Mine Subsidence and Land Conservation Act)

metadata.conditional: Applies only to properties in bituminous coal regions with a severed coal estate; verify via title search.
